Morning all —

I ran three scenarios in our internal sizing model (attached as a sheet). Key assumptions: GPT-like open model variant at 16-bit FP with KV caching available; A100-equivalent baseline single-GPU throughput numbers derived from our bench:
- baseline per-GPU sustained generation: ~1200 tokens/sec (short tokens; with heavy prefix cache this increases for search to ~2400 effective tokens/sec)
- p95 latency per token sequence: 180ms seq-dependent for moderate-length summaries on a single GPU under sustained load

Scenarios (sustained avg tokens/sec demand across cluster):
- Optimistic: 5k tps sustained (cache hit 70%) => effective load ~3.2k tps -> 2 GPUs (1.6k/gpu) with 2x burst headroom => reserve 4 GPUs
- Expected: 12k tps sustained (cache 50%, mixed summaries) => effective load ~9k tps -> 6 GPUs (1.5k/gpu) with 1.5x operational headroom => reserve 9 GPUs
- Conservative: 25k tps sustained (low cache 30%, many long summaries) => effective load ~21k tps -> 18 GPUs required, recommend 22 GPUs for burst/maintenance headroom

Notes on latency SLO fit (95th):
- For interactive flows with cache hits and short responses, p95 <= 250ms achievable on the Expected scenario if request routing prioritizes the interactive pool (lower batching).
- Worst-case long summaries under Conservative will push p95 > 400ms unless we offload to a larger-sequence-optimized model variant (quantized) or accept lower concurrency.

Next steps:
- Rachel: send the scenarios to Alex and ask which usage curve they expect for pilot traffic profiling.
- Karthik: can you provide a quick note on quantization/variant fallback options and cost deltas?

Attachments: freighter_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (sheet with math and GPU-equivalent mapping)

-Marcus

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the call — attached is the revised sheet and a short runbook for ops (SLA-tailored-runbook.pdf). Final recommendation for the pilot (conservative-but-cost-conscious):
- Commit: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (expected to cover Optimistic->low Expected with prefix caching)
- Burst buffer: 5 additional warm GPUs available (auto-burst up to 9 total) to cover 3x short-window spikes while keeping p95 for interactive flows <= 300ms
- Fallback plan: quantized smaller-variant model for long summaries (cost reduction ~30% with 95th latency kept under 450ms for batch-summary jobs)
- Estimated monthly committed cost range (including reserved + modest burst usage): $45k–$72k depending on burst consumption and model variant choices

Why this mix? It minimizes procurement exposure while giving a clear headroom pathway: reserve the baseline expected load, keep warm burst capacity for peaks, and rely on a quantized fallback for long-running workloads. We’ll include explicit rollback/fallback language in the procurement packet and a 30-day initial monitoring window with regression alerts.
